messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PD-8893 fired for #incidents — metering-ingest-consumer-lag. Threshold breached: consumer_lag_seconds > 300 for 2m. Alert burst: 18 events.
Matt S.: acked — I'm oncall. pulling logs now. PD link: https://pagerduty.example/pd/PD-8893
oncall-ops: routing pager to matt.s for this shift.
Carla M. (metering): seeing consumer-group 'metering-ingest-01' lag ~1.2M msgs behind, started at ~01:48 UTC. Throughput spike from 'optimize-eval' producers.
Sophia L. (eng-sre): can we scale consumers ASAP? if backlog > 500k we should enable consumer backpressure and throttle non-billable traffic.
Ben R. (billing): FYI daily billing run at 05:00 UTC. If token counts are underreported we risk invoice discrepancies — recommend preparing manual invoice hold if not resolved in 2h.
Matt S.: scaling now: `kubectl scale deploy metering-consumer -n prod-ingest --replicas=8` (was 3 -> 8). bumping consumer.max.poll.records to 500.
incident-bot: PD-8893 acknowledged by Matt S.
Carla M.: after scale we saw partial catch-up but duplicates remain at dedupe stage. sample SQL: `select count(*) from tokens_staging where duplicate_flag = true and shard = 's12';` => 42,332 duplicates. looks like producer retries (503s) caused dupes.
Sophia L.: can we pause optimize-eval traffic (non-billable) while we stabilize?
Matt S.: applied routing change: `routing-policy reroute optimize-eval -> staging-eval` (applied) — monitoring.
Carla M.: starting dedupe job for affected shards. command: `python infra/scripts/dedupe_tokens.py --shard-start s10 --shard-end s20 --batch 10000` — ETA ~18m.
incident-bot: auto-escalation rule set: if lag > 60s in 20m escalate to eng-pp (lead).
Matt S.: 10m check — lag fell from 720s to 45s. duplicate_count trending down. scaling + reroute working.
Ben R. (billing): opening invoice hold ticket and tagging enterprise customers potentially impacted. setting `invoice_hold=true` on billing-run config until verification.
Carla M.: dedupe finished. uploaded reconciliation snapshot: s3://redwood-ops/recon/reconcile_snapshot_2026-03-14T02:20Z.tar.gz. Token delta summary: median delta 0.2%, 3 accounts > 3% (manual review required).
Matt S.: leaving a postmortem stub and remaining oncall another hour. will close PD if no regressions in 30m.
Ben R. (billing): billing hold will remain until EOD UTC for manual cross-checks with finance and CS.
Carla M.: quick RCA: root cause was a sudden spike of non-billable optimize-eval traffic combined with transient producer retries (503s) that produced duplicate tokens and overwhelmed the consumer group during aggregation window. Mitigations applied: scaled consumers, rerouted eval traffic, ran dedupe/reconciliation, and placed manual invoice hold. Follow-ups: harden producer retry logic (de-dup idempotency), add dedupe at aggregation step, tune alerts to ignore eval-heavy noise, and add a fast-path throttle for non-billable traffic.
Matt S.: thanks all :thumbsup: logging final state to postmortem doc and assigning action items.
incident-bot: PD-8893 closed by Matt S. at 2026-03-14T03:12:10Z
